title: repro_bench.csv freezes 3 to 5 user-style questions per benchmark area, written before any instance runs
goal: kb/public/_retrieval/repro_bench.csv holds 3 to 5 questions per area of repro_briefs.csv, worded as a kb user would ask them, written from the official sources the brief names and not from the kb's own lines, spread over what the kb holds today (present), holds in part (partial) and lacks (absent), each with an expect_re or expect_text that a complete cited answer meets, an area and a stratum column; repro questions passes on it; rag.py eval --file on it prints no REWORD or OFFKB line; no eval run tunes it, and no doc2query expansion, lookup_eval.csv row or lookup_heldout.csv row is made from it; the commit that adds it changes no other file outside kb/_self/backlog/, so the start commit, that commit's parent, holds the briefs and the harness and not the questions.

run:
import os,subprocess,sys
f='kb/public/_retrieval/repro_bench.csv'
if not os.path.exists(f): print('no',f); sys.exit(1)
p=subprocess.run([sys.executable,'_tools/rag.py','eval','--file',f,'--root','public','--all'],capture_output=True,text=True)
out=p.stdout+p.stderr; bad=[l for l in out.splitlines() if l.startswith(('REWORD','OFFKB'))]
print(p.returncode,len(out.splitlines()),bad[:5]); sys.exit(0 if p.returncode in (0,1) and not bad and 'questions=' in out else 1)

import subprocess,sys
f='kb/public/_retrieval/repro_bench.csv'
c=subprocess.run(['git','log','--format=%H','--',f],capture_output=True,text=True,check=True).stdout.split()
if not c: print('not committed'); sys.exit(1)
n=subprocess.run(['git','show','--name-only','--format=','-m',c[-1]],capture_output=True,text=True,check=True).stdout.split()
extra=[x for x in n if x!=f and not x.startswith('kb/_self/backlog/')]
print(len(c),'commit(s)',c[-1],extra); sys.exit(0 if len(c)==1 and not extra else 1)

gates.question: Which expect_verdict does a repro_bench.csv row carry for each stratum (present, partial, absent)?
Does a repro_bench.csv row of the present or partial stratum name the kb article that holds its answer in expect_paths?
options: yes: expect_paths names the article, absent rows leave it empty
no: expect_re only, expect_paths empty on every row
gates.recommendation: yes: expect_paths names the article, absent rows leave it empty
gates.answer: yes: expect_paths names the article, absent rows leave it empty

notes: The questions are written by a worker that sees the briefs and the kb but no research of the instances (none exists yet); held-out style (kb/_self/tools.md answer-rate fitness test; kb/_self/maintaining.md: a failing held-out row stays and is never tuned). False good verdicts today (podman, typescript, rust, python venv) mean an absent-area row needs an expect_re or expect_text, not only a verdict. The start commit for the instances is this file's adding commit's parent (ST-g52zbsv4 setup default). From ST-hfcsyyin's worker (2026-10-15): rag.py eval compares each row's expect_verdict with the pack's verdict, so a repro_bench.csv row with an empty expect_verdict fails the verdict check; set expect_verdict on every row.
